knowledge_point: Finding a Cubic Polynomial Given One Real Root, Two Complex Roots, and a Leading Coefficient
problem: The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2,{x}_{2,3}=1\pm 2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $3.$ Find $f(x).$
worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2,3}=1\pm 2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =3(x-(-2))(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i})) \\  & =3(x+2)(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+2)(x-(1+2\text{i}))(x-(1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 3(x+2)({x}^{2}-x(1+2\text{i})-x(1-2\text{i})+(1+2\text{i})(1-2\text{i})) & = \\ 3(x+2)({x}^{2}-2x+5) & = \\ 3({x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}-4x+5x+10) & = \\ 3({x}^{3}+x+10) & = \\ 3{x}^{3}+3x+30 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=3{x}^{3}+3x+30.$
